subject: Latency windows & fallthrough plan for token-burst benchmark
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acme-analytics.com>, Tim Bates <tim.bates@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency windows & fallthrough plan for token-burst benchmark

Hi Alicia / Tim —

Thanks again for agreeing to run the token-burst benchmarks next week. I want to lock down two things before we finalize calendar invites:

1) The latency windows we should measure (p95/p99 targets at 128/512 tokens).
2) A fallthrough plan if we hit noisy neighbor or GPU preemption (what model variant to fall back to and how to route).

Proposed slots (PST):
- Tue 2026-10-06 10:30–12:00 — baseline single-model run (no batching)
- Tue 2026-10-06 14:00–16:00 — burst runs (aggressive concurrent clients)
- Wed 2026-10-07 09:00–11:00 — canary + failover validation (small sample)

Ask: please confirm which slot works for your infra team and attach any existing runbooks or token profiles. We’ll bring a small Redwood ops pod (Karthik + Marissa) and a perf observer (Dylan).

Agenda (30/90/60 min split):
- 30m: test harness, traffic shape, and KV cache settings
- 90m: two pass runs (baseline → burst) with live latency dashboards
- 60m: root-cause & mitigation playbook, fallback verification

I attached our standard token profile template — fill in peak TPS and expected concurrency if possible.

Thanks,
Soojin
So I Lee
Senior Product Manager, Performance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_token_profile.csv (CSV stub)
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acme-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Bates <tim.bates@acme-analytics.com>, perf-eng@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency windows & fallthrough plan for token-burst benchmark

On Fri, Oct 2, 2026 at 09:12 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alicia / Tim —
> 
> Thanks again for agreeing to run the token-burst benchmarks next week. I want to lock down two things before we finalize calendar invites:...

Thanks Soojin — we can do Tue 10/06 for the baseline + burst windows and Wed 10/07 for the canary; the proposed times work for our infra team.

Attached our current token profile and a short runbook (internal) — note the following constraints:
- Our cluster has a nightly eviction window from 03:00–04:00 UTC (not relevant for your slots but FYI).
- Peak concurrency expected: 420 concurrent streams at 128 tokens.
- We have a lightweight L7 proxy that can throttle clients by route; we can flip a canary route to the fallback variant.

We prefer to fallback to the quantized LLM-q2 variant if throughput falloff > 25% and p99 latency increases > 40% relative to baseline. That should preserve semantics while reducing GPU memory pressure.

I’ll upload the runbook as a PDF in a follow-up and add the perf-eng alias to the invite.

—Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Analytics

Attachments: acme_runbook_v2.pdf (PDF stub)
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com, Alicia Gomez <alicia@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency windows & fallthrough plan for token-burst benchmark

Soojin — quick internal note before we confirm calendar:

- Resource constraints: one of our Dedicated pools has a maintenance reservation on Wed 10/07 08:30–10:30 PST for infra patching. That overlaps the proposed canary window. I recommend we shift the canary to Wed 10/07 11:00–13:00 PST to ensure we have clean nodes.
- Observability: Marissa, can you prepare a dashboard with the following series: p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, queue depth, KV cache hit rate, and gRPC retry counts? Prefer to have them ready 30m before the run.
- Fallback policy: If we flip to LLM-q2, we should also test sample output equivalence on 50 synthetic prompts to validate quality delta. Dylan — can you own the A/B sample set and quick diff script?

If Acme confirms the time shift for Wed, I’ll update the invite and attach the dashboard link.

Thanks — Karthik

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acme-analytics.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency windows & fallthrough plan for token-burst benchmark

Thanks — Wed 10/07 11:00–13:00 PST works for us. I appreciate the heads-up about the maintenance window.

I’ve uploaded the runbook and token profile to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRunbookV2 and added the perf-eng alias to the invite. We’ll also provision a small tracing span on our side so you can cross-check tail latency traces.

One last ask: during the burst run, if we see p99 > 1.5s at 128 tokens, we’ll trigger the fallback and immediately run the synthetic 50-sample diff. That should give us a quick quality gauge before deciding to route permanently.

See you on Tue for the baseline run. —Alicia
